html:
SMTO-HTTP-0016 — Access to the web service was not granted

GUID: bd8db44c-0c90-403e-b9ff-ff207ae9d35b
Slug: http-oauth-denied
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • When SMTO asked permission to use your account on the web service, the request was declined, so SMTO couldn't connect. SMTO did not use the service with your account.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you meant to allow access, ask SMTO to connect to the service again. When the prompt appears, select Open authorization page and approve the access on the service's page. The earlier permission request was declined and can't be reused, so a new one is needed.
  2. On the service's page, sign in with the account SMTO should use, and check whether your organization requires an administrator to approve new apps. Some services decline access automatically when the account isn't allowed to approve apps.
  3. If you didn't want SMTO to use this service, no fix is needed; tell SMTO in the conversation to continue without it. Declining is a valid choice, and SMTO won't use the account without your approval.

What success looks like

  • The sign-in prompt disappears and SMTO continues the task using the service.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or your account administrator. Never put passwords, codes or access tokens in the conversation, screenshots or error reports.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • OAuth authorization was denied: the provider returned access_denied, or the authorization callback for this connection recorded a denial.

What this means

  • OAuth returned access_denied, or the owned authorization transaction recorded denial. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • OAuth returned access_denied, or the owned authorization transaction recorded denial.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the current authorization transaction's denial state without assuming a password was wrong.

How to fix it

  • OAuth2.accept maps an access_denied token response, and http_session_state.prepare maps a callback recorded as denied, to this error. Start a fresh authorization only if the user intends to grant consent; if consent keeps failing, check the provider's consent or admin-approval policy and the requested scopes.
  • Start a fresh supported authorization flow only if the user intends to grant access.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • An intentionally restarted authorization flow obtains the user's intended consent.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
